fig01_storage_level.png: Weekly working gas in storage (EIA series NW2_EPG0_SWO_R48_BCF, current vintage). The saw-tooth pattern is the annual injection (spring-autumn) and withdrawal (winter) cycle.
fig02_weekly_change.png: Weekly storage change, S_t - S_(t-1). Positive = net injection; negative = net withdrawal.
fig03_seasonal_change.png: Distribution of weekly storage changes by calendar month. Boxes span the middle 50%; the line is the median. A change that is normal in one month is extreme in another, so anomalies are measured against a seasonal baseline.
fig04_henry_hub_price.png: FRED series DHHNGSP (source: EIA/Refinitiv). Gaps are market holidays or missing reports. The y-axis starts at zero to avoid exaggerating moves.
fig05_return_distribution.png: One-day forward log returns from the first eligible post-release price (development sample). n = 491.
fig06_anomaly_distribution.png: Point-in-time standardized storage anomaly, expanding-mean method (development sample). n = 491.
fig07_scatter_z_return.png: Each dot is one release week (development sample); the line joins decile averages. n = 491. Association is not causation.
fig08_quintile_returns.png: Q1 = most negative anomalies (less gas than normal), Q5 = most positive. Error bars: 95% block-bootstrap intervals. Quintile cut points use the whole development sample, so this is descriptive, not a tradable rule.
fig09_absz_quintile_vol.png: Q1 = smallest absolute anomalies, Q5 = largest. Error bars: 95% block-bootstrap intervals.
fig10_correlation.png: Pearson correlations among features and targets in the development sample. Correlation is not causation.
fig11_sample_counts.png: Weeks with a valid anomaly and 1-day target. Early years are lost to the minimum-history requirement.
fig12_event_groups_dev.png: Groups use fixed thresholds on point-in-time Z (-1.5, -0.5, +0.5, +1.5). Error bars: 95% block-bootstrap intervals. H1 predicts bars falling from left to right.
fig13_car_paths_dev.png: Average cumulative log return measured from the last daily price before the release (day 0). The shaded span covers the release: day 1 is usually the release day itself, whose daily price mixes pre- and post-release trades; day 2 is usually the first tradable price. Daily data say nothing about intraday timing. Only the extreme groups and the middle group are drawn for legibility.
fig14_m1_residuals.png: Left: a funnel shape would indicate heteroskedasticity. Right: bars outside the dashed approximate 95% band indicate serial correlation. Both motivate Newey-West standard errors.
fig15_m1_stability.png: Each point re-estimates the univariate regression using all data up to the year shown. A coefficient whose sign or size wanders, or whose band always straddles zero, is not stable evidence.
fig16_backtest_validation.png: Spot-price simulation, not an executable strategy. Costs: 10 bps + 5 bps slippage per side; holding 1 trading day(s).
fig17_direction_calibration_test.png: Logistic model on Z, refitted on train+validation; quintile buckets of predicted probability.
